_doc: Pod kinds registry. Each pod 'kind' field used in the codebase has an entry here describing what it is, whether it auto-mirrors to the KG, and how its body gets populated. Adding a new kind is a config edit; the kg_mirror dispatcher reads this on every pod write.
_canonical_example: Append a new entry to 'kinds' as a starting point for a new pod kind. See skills/extending-emi-pod-kinds/SKILL.md for the field reference.

image.description: Image artifact (PNG/JPEG/etc). Stored content-addressed under data/images/<sha>.<ext>. Body is populated by the vision-extraction pass (caption + OCR).

email.description: Inbound email. one_liner=subject, body=email body verbatim. Source refs back to the event_repository row.
email._doc_excluded_from_kg: Email content is noisy, sensitive, and token-heavy. Excluded by design until an attribution/extraction policy lands.

chat_cluster.description: Resolved chat segment from pod_classifier with entity-anchored sections. Body is the resolved markdown sections.

service_loop.description: Internal pod_classifier service-loop placeholder. Not user-facing content; emitted to keep the pipeline running when there's nothing to classify.

_doc_chat_introduced: Pod source_kind values that ALWAYS auto-mirror to the KG regardless of the pod's kind. The principle: when the user introduces a pod into chat (uploaded a file, pasted an image, asked Emi to mint one from disk), the pod is part of the conversation and must be KG-addressable so extracted relationships can edge into it. Email-sourced pods intentionally do NOT trigger this — they go through the normal allow list.
